h1: The 7 Best AT&T Cordless Phones of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best AT&T Cordless Phones: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven AT&T cordless phones from one-handset basics to five-handset office systems, with call blocking and cell link notes.
summary: The AT&T DL72479 is the best AT&T cordless phone for most homes, bundling four handsets, a smart call blocker and Bluetooth Connect to Cell for $50 to $100. The DLP73590 suits home offices with a 5 inch screen and conference calling. The BL102 is the cheapest route to call blocking.
intro: AT&T sells a lot of near-identical cordless phones, and the model numbers do little to explain the gap between them. The practical divide is how many handsets you get, whether the call blocker is smart or basic, and whether a Bluetooth link to your mobile is included. Everything else, from the DECT 6.0 radio to the answering machine, is nearly the same across the line.

We reviewed eight AT&T systems and kept seven, leaving out a close sibling with the same feature set. The ranking weighs handset count, call blocking type, cell link, display and extras such as conference calling, using spec sheets and owner feedback instead of lab work. Price buckets matter here, because the cheapest and dearest models do not differ by as much as the bucket jump implies.

products.name: AT&T DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone, 4-Handset, Smart Call Blocker, Bluetooth Connect to Cell, Caller ID Announce, Answering Machine - DL72479
products.verdict: Four handsets, smart blocking and a cell link at a fair bucket.
products.description:
The DL72479 ships with four handsets and an answering machine, plus a smart call blocker that screens unknown callers, spoken caller names and a Bluetooth link to your mobile. The smart blocker is the feature that earns its place, since it stops robocalls from ringing every handset in the house. Bluetooth Connect to Cell then brings mobile calls to the same handsets.

It leads because the combination costs $50 to $100. The BL102-4 also supplies four handsets, but sits in the $100 to $200 bucket and has no cell link. The DLP73590 adds screen size and conference calling, but at a higher price and for a use case most households never need.

Buy it for a multi-room family home. The caveat is that the listing mentions no color display, so handset screens are plainer than the BL108 or DLP73590. It also lacks conference calling.
products.idealFor: Families wanting phones in several rooms.

products.name: AT&T 5-Handset DECT 6.0 Cordless Home and Business Phone with Answering Machine, 5" Color Display, One-Touch Shortcut, Conference, Intercom, Smart Call Blocker, Bluetooth Connect to Cell - DLP73590
products.verdict: Five handsets, a 5 inch screen and conference calling.
products.description:
The DLP73590 comes with five handsets, a 5 inch color display, conference calling, intercom, an answering machine, a smart call blocker and Bluetooth Connect to Cell. A 5 inch color display is large enough to browse a phone book and read caller names without squinting. Conference calling is the feature that sets it apart from every other AT&T here.

It ranks second because it sits in the $100 to $200 bucket, a bucket above the DL72479, and most households will never join a conference call from a landline. For a home office the extras justify the cost, and it carries five handsets to the DL72479's four.

Buy it if you work from home and take business calls regularly. The caveat is price and scope: families who just want spam filtering and multi-room phones pay for features they will not touch.
products.idealFor: Home offices that run phone calls.
products.skipIf: You only need basic home use.

products.name: AT&T DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone, Smart Call Blocker, Bluetooth Connect to Cell, Answering Machine, 2.4" Color Display, Big Buttons - BL108
products.verdict: A color screen, big buttons and a cell link in one handset set.
products.description:
The BL108 pairs a 2.4 inch color display with big buttons, a smart call blocker, Bluetooth Connect to Cell and an answering machine. Big buttons combined with a color screen make it easier to read for anyone with imperfect eyesight, and it still has the same smart blocker as the top pick.

It ranks third because it matches the DL72479 on key features at the same $50 to $100 bucket, yet the listing never states the handset count. That uncertainty matters, since a household that wants phones in three rooms needs to know how many handsets arrive. It also trails the DLP73590 on screen size, at 2.4 inches against 5.

Buy it for a couple or an apartment where one or two handsets are enough. The caveat is verification: confirm the number of handsets in the box before you order.
products.skipIf: You need phones in many rooms.

products.name: AT&T BL102-4 DECT 6.0 4-Handset Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, Call Blocking, Caller ID Announcer, Audio Assist, Intercom, and Unsurpassed Range
products.verdict: Four handsets with audio assist but no Bluetooth link.
products.description:
The BL102-4 provides four handsets, call blocking, an answering machine, a caller ID announcer, audio assist and an intercom, in the $100 to $200 bucket. Audio assist is the distinguishing feature: it boosts volume for hard-to-hear calls, which helps older users with mild hearing loss.

It ranks fourth because it sits a bucket above the DL72479 and omits the Bluetooth cell link that the DL72479 includes, while the blocking is described as plain call blocking and not smart blocking. For landline-only households it is a fine fit, but the DL72479 gives more for less.

Buy it for a larger home that still relies on a landline and values audio assist. The caveat is the missing Bluetooth link, so mobile calls will not reach the handsets.
products.skipIf: You want to pair a mobile.

products.name: AT&T TL88102BK DECT 6.0 2-Line Expandable Cordless Phone with Answering System and Dual Caller ID/Call Waiting, 3 Handsets, Black
products.verdict: Handles two phone lines across three handsets.
products.description:
The TL88102BK is a two-line expandable system with three handsets, dual caller ID with call waiting, and an answering system. Two-line support is rare in cordless phones: it lets one base manage two separate numbers, so a small business can take calls on both without a second phone.

It ranks fifth because very few buyers run two lines, and it sits in the $200 to $500 bucket, the most expensive in this group. It also lists no Bluetooth cell link or smart blocker in our data. If you do run two lines, it is the right choice, because nothing else here handles them.

Buy it for a small office or home business with two numbers. The caveat is relevance: a single-line home pays a premium for a capability it never uses, and the DL72479 does more for far less.

products.name: AT&T EL52113 Cordless Phone with Answering System and Extra-Large Backlit Keys, Light Champagne
products.verdict: Extra-large backlit keys on a single handset.
products.description:
The EL52113 has extra-large backlit keys, an answering system and one handset, in a light champagne finish, at $25 to $50. The large backlit keys are a real accessibility feature: they let users with limited vision or dexterity dial without errors, even in a dim room.

It ranks sixth because no call blocking or cell link is listed, and it comes with a single handset. In a world of constant spam calls, that leaves the user exposed. The BL102 at the same bucket at least adds call blocking, though it has a standard keypad.

Buy it for a parent or grandparent who struggles with small dial pads. The caveat is spam: with no blocking listed, expect unwanted calls to ring through unless the carrier filters them.
products.idealFor: People who need big dialing keys.

products.name: AT&T BL102 DECT 6.0 Cordless Phone for Home with Answering Machine, Call Blocking, Caller ID Announcer, Audio Assist, Intercom, and Unsurpassed Range
products.verdict: The cheapest way into AT&T call blocking and audio assist.
products.description:
The BL102 includes one handset, an answering machine, call blocking, a caller ID announcer and audio assist, at $25 to $50. It is the lowest bucket in the group and still carries blocking and audio assist.

It ranks last because it has only one handset and no cell link, so it cannot cover a whole house. Against the EL52113 at the same bucket, it adds call blocking and audio assist but loses the extra-large backlit keys. The cost of expansion also adds up if you later want more handsets.

Buy it for a single room, a guest bedroom or a small apartment where one phone is enough. The caveat is growth: expanding needs extra handsets, and for a multi-room home the DL72479 offers four handsets for not much more.

whatMatters.detail: Each handset is a phone you can place in another room, all registered to one base. More handsets raise the price, and the number varies even within one model line. Count the rooms where you actually answer calls, plus the ones you may add later, then check the handset number in the title. The BL108 listing leaves the count unclear, so confirm it.

Smart call blockers screen unknown numbers before they ring, so spam calls never reach your handsets. Basic blocking only stops numbers you add to a list. If spam arrives daily, smart blocking saves real annoyance. The DL72479 and BL108 list smart call blocker, while the BL102 and BL102-4 list plain call blocking.

Connect to Cell pairs your mobile by Bluetooth so calls ring on the home handsets. It helps where indoor signal is weak, and it lets you use one answering setup for both numbers. The DL72479, DLP73590 and BL108 list it. Confirm the phrase Bluetooth Connect to Cell in the title before you buy, and make sure your mobile supports Bluetooth pairing.

Most homes have one phone line, but some offices have two. A two-line system manages both numbers from one base. The TL88102BK is the only two-line model here. If you have one line, extra capacity adds cost without benefit. Check how many lines your provider supplies before choosing, and ask whether you truly need both numbers on one base.

Larger keys and displays help users with poor eyesight. The EL52113 has extra-large backlit keys, the BL108 has big buttons, and the DLP73590 has a 5 inch color display. Look for the screen size in inches and descriptors like big or extra-large buttons, and consider who will actually use the phone every day.

faq.q: Are AT&T handsets interchangeable between models?
faq.a: Not always. Handsets generally pair with their own base, so a DL72479 handset may not work with a BL102 base. Check compatibility in the manual before mixing models, and buy matching expansion handsets from the same series.

Most need a phone jack for a landline. Models with Connect to Cell, like the DL72479 and BL108, can also link to your mobile over Bluetooth, though they are designed to work alongside a landline, not replace the base unit.

It boosts volume for hard-to-hear calls, which helps users with mild hearing loss. The BL102 and BL102-4 list it. If hearing is a concern, check the volume range in the manual too, and test it in a quiet room.

faq.q: How do I block a number?
faq.a: Use the call block menu on the handset to add a number. Smart blockers like the one on the DL72479 also screen unknown callers on their own, so you spend less time maintaining a block list.

faq.q: How long do the batteries last?
faq.a: Rechargeable handset batteries decline over several years. Replace them with the type named in the manual when talk time drops. Keeping handsets in the charging cradle when not in use is normal for all these models.

Some systems are expandable. The TL88102BK is listed as expandable, and DECT bases generally support a fixed number of handsets, so check the base's maximum number of registered handsets before buying extras.

finalTake: Buy the DL72479 for a family home: four handsets, smart blocking and a cell link in the $50 to $100 bucket. Home offices should step up to the DLP73590 for conference calling. Choose the TL88102BK only if you really run two lines, and keep the EL52113 for people who need large keys more than features.
